#D.Scale_Dist_Dev         0.2212846  0.08839817    0.04802738   0.3945418

This produces an estimate of N of 466.

My next model is:

#D.Scale_dist_BISO     -1.5821775 0.2692391  -2.10987643  -1.0544787
#D.Scale_Dist_Dev        0.2782765 0.0953368   0.09141977   0.4651332
#g0                                 -5.7077016 0.6848632  -7.05000876  -4.3653943
#g0.bkTRUE                   2.4278227 0.5378224   1.37371014   3.4819352
#g0.h22                          4.0001992 0.7589132   2.51275671   5.4876418
#sigma                           9.0219603 0.1969722   8.63590198   9.4080187
#sigma.h22                  -1.9386642 0.2225860  -2.37492469  -1.5024036
#pmix.h22                     1.0794725 0.9479146  -0.77840606   2.9373511

which has a deltaAIC of about 2 and produces an estimate of 407.  This was based on 74 detections of 155 bears at 129 detectors (g0~1= 0.2). I used a finite mixture model for both g0 and sigma.  My question is, how concerned should I be that the top model has a high SE for the g0.bkTRUE parameter (beta=13.4820598, SE=64.45658833)?  Should I throw out the top model and use only the second or should I model average?  Thanks!
Joe

messages.author: 118cea91a1619106
messages.subject: Re: finite mixtures and imprecise parameter estimate
parts:
Hi Joe
My guess is that the large estimate of SE arises because the estimate is on the boundary (invlogit(-5.7975810 + 13.4820598) = 0.9995403) and should not be a worry in itself.
Model averaging seems desirable given the divergence in N-hat. I recently had trouble with model averaging a boundary estimate on the link scale - probably you will want to model average on the real scale (against the usual advice).
Murray

On Monday, November 29, 2021 at 2:47:57 PM UTC-5 murray...@gmail.com wrote:
Hi Joe
My guess is that the large estimate of SE arises because the estimate is on the boundary (invlogit(-5.7975810 + 13.4820598) = 0.9995403) and should not be a worry in itself.
Model averaging seems desirable given the divergence in N-hat. I recently had trouble with model averaging a boundary estimate on the link scale - probably you will want to model average on the real scale (against the usual advice).
Murray
